newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares sink in nervous U.S.-led trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares sink in nervous U.S.-led trade.

text.p: German shares fell on Thursday as tension mounted ahead of the release of key U.S. economic data and as disappointing interim results from BASF sparked a rout on heavyweight chemical shares.
The 30-share DAX index ended the bourse session down 47.05 points, or 1.10 percent, at 4,231.43 points.
Prices weakened still further in nervous afternoon electronic trade, with the IBIS DAX index ending the day at 4,195.53 points, below a psychologically key 4,200 point level.

Dealers said fears of imminent interest rate hikes continued to pressure the market in post-bourse trade, even after the eagerly awaited U.S. jobless claims and consumer price data landed in line with forecasts.
The chemical sector was the biggest drag on the market. The chemical sector index, based on stocks in the broader DAX 100 index, registered a drop of 2.9 percent.
"The chemicals were really out today," said one trader.
"Hoechst (interim results) were not particularly good and now BASF had no ace up its sleeve either."

BASF posted six-month net profit of 1.42 billion marks, up 3.4 percent and at the lower end of expectations. That followed an earnings report from Hoechst earlier this week which showed operating profits fell 18 percent.

Meanwhile the market was saved from dramatic losses by a sharp advance in shares in utility group RWE, which was boosted by plans to scrap the multiple voting rights that give local municipalities control of a chunk of its shares.
RWE ended the bourse session up seven marks, or nearly nine percent, at 87 marks.
The company's voting rights move is viewed as opening up the company to international investors by loosening the hold municipalities have on its equity.

BASF fell 3.53 marks, or 4.9 percent, to 68.67 marks while rival Hoechst dropped 4.90 marks, or six percent, to 76.10 marks in bourse trade. Bayer, the last of the big three chemical groups, dropped 1.55 marks to 74.25 marks.
